note: Items taken from the fact-checked daily report of 2026-10-04 (and the ASML deep dive); written 2026-10-05.

STRL.what: Jumped 5.6% with no company news: the whole market and construction stocks rose after a weak jobs report made an interest-rate rise less likely, and STRL usually moves about three times as much as the market.

Q2 revenue $1.168bn (+90%), backlog $4.33bn (+116%), 2026 outlook raised to $4.00-4.15bn; yet the stock fell 13% after hours, possibly because the extra revenue comes at lower margins (inference, medium confidence).
Filed a shelf registration (S-3) that lets it sell new shares quickly whenever it chooses; none sold so far, but the stock fell 8.3% that week.

CRWD.what: President Michael Sentonas sold about $64.2m of shares (about 16% of his direct stake) under a 10b5-1 plan, a selling schedule set in advance.
Put Falcon on the OpenAI Marketplace, so OpenAI business customers can pay for it from their OpenAI budgets.
The chief financial officer sold about $125.5m of shares under a pre-planned plan; insiders sold about $210m in a few weeks and bought nothing.
Security stocks surged after AI-lab leaders warned about the risks of powerful AI (Forbes headline: CrowdStrike +14%).
Q2: ARR $5.84bn (+25%), revenue $1.47bn (+26%), record net new ARR $332.8m (+51%); full-year revenue forecast raised to $5,991-6,011m. Standard (GAAP) profit only $5.3m.

source.name: CrowdStrike Q2 FY2027 results (Yahoo Finance copy)

MRNA.what: Nasdaq said Moderna joins the Nasdaq-100 index before the open on 2026-10-09; index funds must buy shares, but the business is unchanged.
Citi downgraded to Sell and sees the stock at $80, arguing the price already assumes about $13bn a year of cancer-vaccine sales.
Named Juan Andres to a new Chief Operating Officer role from 2026-10-05; the chief technical operations and quality officer will retire. The CEO and CFO stay.
Raised $3.0bn with convertible bonds: they could become about 14 million new shares (about 3.6% more) above about $210.58; a capped-call hedge offsets that up to about $392.62.
Moderna and Merck's personalised melanoma vaccine (intismeran) plus Keytruda met its main goal in a Phase 3 trial (the final round of patient testing before approval). The stock rose 177% that day.
The FDA approved mFLUSIVA, Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine, for adults 50 and over.
Q2 revenue $145m and a net loss of $0.8bn: today's business (mostly COVID vaccines) is small and loss-making.

CRDO.what: The chief operating officer sold 50,000 shares (about $10.3m) under a pre-planned 10b5-1 plan; insiders sold about $41.5m from 2026-09-23 to 10-02, all flagged as pre-planned, and bought nothing.
After the results, BofA (to $275 from $340) and JPMorgan (to $310 from $335) cut their price targets, and Mizuho did too later in September; none lowered its rating.

Q1 revenue $479.0m (+114.7%), above forecasts; next quarter guided to $525-535m and full-year growth above 85%. But the standard gross margin fell to 64.5% from 68.2%, and the stock fell about 20% the next day (margin drop the likely cause, inference).
Completed its purchase of DustPhotonics, expanding into optical chips.

LITE.what: Record close of $1,085.42 (+3.79%), mostly because chip stocks rose. After the close a filing showed the CFO sold 24,542 shares (about $25.7m, roughly a quarter of his stake) under a pre-planned 10b5-1 plan.
Bernstein started covering optical stocks at Outperform; Lumentum jumped 7.7% as the group rallied.
US senators introduced a bill to keep Chinese optical transceivers out of US national-security systems, which could help US makers. Not law.
The annual report (10-K) showed Lumentum swapped convertible bonds for about 10.6 million new shares, about 13% more shares in the quarter: less debt, but each owner's slice is smaller.
Q4 revenue doubled to $1.01bn (+109%); next quarter guided to $1.225-1.275bn; management said it is still shipping behind customer demand for its lasers.
Signed a six-year deal reserving production at AXT (wafer maker for lasers), backed by two $43.5m deposits, securing a scarce input.

TSM.what: Bloomberg reported TSMC is weighing a multi-factory campus near Dallas, each factory costing at least $20bn; early stage, and TSMC said "no comment on market rumors".
August sales were a record NT$514.81bn (New Taiwan dollars), up 53.3% from a year earlier, driven by AI chips.
Q2 revenue US$40.20bn (+36%) with a 67.7% gross margin; Q3 guided to US$44.6-45.8bn, with margin guided slightly lower (65-67%) because new 2-nanometre factories cost more at first.

AMD.what: Rose 2.95% to a record close, almost all because the market and chip stocks rose.
Agreed to buy World Labs, Fei-Fei Li's AI lab, for about $8.2bn paid only in AMD shares (about 0.8% more shares, researcher's calculation); the stock fell 3.6% that day.
CEO Lisa Su sold about $48.1m of shares under a pre-planned 10b5-1 plan.
Q2 revenue $11.5bn (+50%), data center $6.7bn (+107%); Q3 guided to about $13.0bn (+41%). The stock still fell 7% afterwards.

Anthropic agreed to deploy up to 2 gigawatts of AMD GPUs in AMD's Helios racks, first gigawatt from the first half of 2027; AMD committed to invest up to $5bn in Anthropic. (Anthropic makes Claude, which wrote this file.)

PANW.what: TD Cowen raised its price target to $440 from $400 and kept a Buy rating (an opinion, not new facts).
Lee Klarich gave away 25,000 shares as a gift, not a sale.
Launched new AI-security services such as Unit 42 Frontier AI Defense.
Bernstein lowered its rating, saying the stock had run past fair value.
Security stocks jumped (PANW about +13%) after AI-lab leaders warned about the risks of powerful AI, which investors read as more security spending ahead.

Q4 revenue $3.41bn (+34%), above forecasts; next-generation security ARR $9.10bn (+63%). Next year's forecast $14.10-14.20bn means growth slows to 23-24% as the CyberArk boost fades; standard (GAAP) loss of $0.35 a share.
Completed the purchase of CyberArk (logins and passwords for people and AI agents) for $21.1bn, paid partly with 112 million new shares.

BE.what: Barclays raised its target to $308 and kept a neutral rating, citing a second factory in Fremont, California, and utility demand (Ameren plans 500 megawatts of fuel cells).
Virginia's 2026 Energy Plan named fuel cells as a near-term clean-power option (Bloom not named); fuel-cell stocks rallied the next day and BE rose 4.17%.

Oracle invoked force majeure (a claim that events outside its control excuse a delay) on Project Jupiter in New Mexico, which may use up to 2.45 gigawatts of Bloom fuel cells, because the gas pipeline slipped to February 2027. All sides say the contract stands.
Shareholders filed a securities class action after a Hunterbrook report on Chinese scandium (a rare metal) in Bloom's supply chain, which Bloom calls false.
Q2 revenue $1,065.4m (+165.5%) with $226.4m of operating cash flow; 2026 outlook raised to $3.9-4.2bn.

SNOW.what: Closed the sale of $3.75bn of 0% convertible notes (loans paying no interest that lenders can swap for shares, at about $500.38 and $483.98); a hedge limits dilution up to $820.30. If converted, about 2.2% more shares (up to about 4%). First announced 2026-09-28.

Product revenue $1,491.9m (+37%), a third quarter in a row of faster growth; net revenue retention 126%; the stock jumped 22%. Contracted future revenue slipped from $9.21bn to $9.00bn, and the standard (GAAP) loss was $191.7m.
A securities class action (shareholders saying they were misled) was filed against the former CEO and former CFO; Snowflake's motion to dismiss is due 2026-10-13 (10-Q).

AAOI.what: Jumped 7.71% on Friday (and 8.1% on Thursday) with no company news, as optical-networking stocks rose together.
Set up a program to sell up to $600m of new shares over time, its third this year; the stock fell 13.8% the next trading day.
The 10-Q showed shares outstanding rose from 75.0m to 84.4m in six months; top 10 customers are 99% of revenue; customers owe $314.0m, $211.0m of it from one distributor; GAAP net loss $22.8m.
Record Q2 revenue $191.9m (+86.4%), data centers 56.1%, first adjusted profit; Q3 guided to $255-290m; building capacity for about 650,000 high-speed units a month by end-2026.

A.what: Rose 0.66% with no company news; the past week's fall was mostly health-care stocks falling.
Declared a dividend of 25.5 cents a share (record date 2026-10-06, paid 2026-10-28).
UBS lowered its rating to Neutral with a $165 price target.
Q3 revenue $1.88bn and adjusted profit $1.62 a share, both above forecasts; yearly forecast raised. $0.06 of the profit was a one-time tariff refund; core growth +7.3%.

AXTI.what: Scheduled its Q3 results for 2026-10-29 after the US close.
The 10-Q said China's export permits for indium phosphide wafers to US customers are still not issued, which AXT calls "the most significant challenge we currently face".
Lumentum signed a six-year deal reserving AXT's production, backed by two $43.5m deposits.
The CEO (about $22.3m) and three directors sold shares without pre-planned plans, which would have met your "several insiders" breaker at the time.
Sold 8.56 million new shares at $64.25, raising the share count about 15%.

VIAV.what: Rose 5.18%, its 13th higher close in a row, with no company news; optical peers also rose and call-option buying (bets on further gains) was heavy.
Bernstein started covering optical-networking stocks at Outperform and Coherent launched a new optics platform; the group rose 7-11% and VIAVI 6.8%.
Between 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-11 three insiders (two directors and an executive) sold about $4.2m of shares without a pre-planned plan; the largest was a director's ~$3.27m on 2026-08-17.
Q4 revenue $443.1m (+52.5%), above its own guidance; next quarter guided to $450-460m; the shares still fell, which coverage linked to dilution from the May share sale.
Announced a public offering; it sold about 12.8 million new shares at $45, raising the share count about 15% in a year.

FORM.what: Barely moved (+0.48%) while chip stocks rose; its own small dip was normal noise and no reason was published.
S&P moves FormFactor from the SmallCap 600 into the MidCap 400 index before the open on 2026-10-06; index funds rebalance, but the business is unchanged.
Deutsche Bank began coverage positively, saying FormFactor is now a second approved supplier of test cards for NVIDIA graphics chips; the stock rose 9.6%.
Memory maker Micron reported quarterly revenue of $54.23bn against $51.07bn expected, a sign the AI-memory boom (FormFactor's main market) continues.
Record Q2 revenue $258.2m (+31.9%) and adjusted gross margin 53.3%; Q3 guided to $270m plus or minus $10m. Management said about a third of the margin gain was one-off.

ASML.what: Rose 3.25% to $1,867.31, mostly because chip stocks rallied; no ASML news.

Dutch prime minister lobbied the US against the MATCH Act, a proposed US law that would stop ASML selling older machines to Chinese chipmakers and servicing those already there. Not law; status unconfirmed.
Morgan Stanley reportedly cut its price target to EUR 1,700 from EUR 1,930 (still positive), worried about China demand and margins.
Samsung reportedly deepened its partnership on High-NA EUV, ASML's newest machine, aiming to use it for memory chips by 2028. No order size given; not confirmed by a primary source.
Q2 beat expectations (sales EUR 9.3bn, profit EUR 2.9bn); 2026 sales forecast raised to EUR 43-45bn from EUR 36-40bn, the second raise this year; 2027 EUV capacity nearly fully booked.
TSMC, ASML's biggest customer, said it has no plans to use High-NA EUV machines through 2029 because they are "very, very expensive".

MRNA.event: Joins the Nasdaq-100 index before the open
Full melanoma trial data at the ESMO cancer conference

LITE.event: OCP Global Summit (data-center hardware conference); Lumentum talks 2026-10-14

TSM.event: Q3 2026 results, 2:00 a.m. US Eastern (guidance US$44.6-45.8bn)

AMD.event: Lisa Su keynote at the OCP Global Summit

BE.event: Gas pipeline for Oracle's Project Jupiter expected

SNOW.event: Court deadline: Snowflake's motion to dismiss the 2026 class action

A.event: Dividend record date (25.5 cents a share; paid 2026-10-28)

AXTI.event: Q3 2026 results, after the US close (guidance about $66m, tier 3)

FORM.event: Joins the S&P MidCap 400 index before the open

ASML.event: Q3 2026 results (company expects EUR 11.0-12.0bn sales, 55-57% gross margin)
TSMC Q3 results (ASML's biggest customer; factory-spending plans)
US defence bill (NDAA) timetable: possible inclusion of the MATCH Act
